jobs.title: Executive Director of Behavioral Health Development
jobs.description:
Phoenix Transitional Housing Plus (PTHP)
is seeking an experienced healthcare and behavioral health executive or consultant to lead the development and launch of a new behavioral health services division focused on transition-age youth and young adults.
This is not a full-time employment position.
This is a project-based contractual engagement for an experienced professional who has previously taken a California Medi-Cal behavioral health program through the process of development, application/certification or approval, implementation, and successful operational launch.
The Opportunity Phoenix is an established California nonprofit organization providing transitional housing and comprehensive supportive services to transition-age youth and young adults.
We are now preparing for the next stage of our development: establishing an integrated behavioral health program capable of providing high-quality mental health services while complementing our existing housing, case management, education, employment, and independent-living programs.
Our initial objective is to evaluate, develop, and pursue the appropriate pathway for Phoenix to provide California Medi-Cal Specialty Mental Health Services (SMHS)
and related behavioral health services.
We are seeking someone who has already successfully navigated this process
and can lead Phoenix from concept through operational deployment.
REQUIRED EXPERIENCE Applicants must have direct, demonstrated experience
leading the development and launch of a California Medi-Cal mental health or behavioral health program.
Candidates must be able to demonstrate previous responsibility for activities such as:
Writing and preparing behavioral health certification, approval, enrollment, or contracting applications.
Successfully submitting applications and supporting documentation to applicable California and/or county regulatory agencies.
Navigating California Medi-Cal behavioral health requirements.
Working with county behavioral health agencies and/or the California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS).
Responding to regulatory questions, corrective actions, deficiencies, or requests for additional documentation.
Developing policies and procedures required for program approval and operation.
Developing clinical and administrative workflows.
Establishing Medi-Cal-compliant documentation and billing systems.
Developing quality assurance, compliance, utilization management, and risk-management systems.
Recruiting and structuring appropriate clinical and administrative staffing.
Preparing an organization for certification, readiness reviews, audits, or site reviews.
Taking a behavioral health program from planning through actual operational launch
.
Managing or providing executive oversight of a Medi-Cal-funded behavioral health program after implementation.

Applicants whose experience is limited to working within an already-established mental health program will not meet the minimum experience requirement for this engagement.

Phoenix specifically seeks someone who has participated at the executive or project-lead level in building, obtaining approval for, and launching a program.

Scope of Engagement The selected contractor will work directly with Phoenix's Chief Executive Officer and leadership team and will be expected to:
Conduct an organizational and regulatory readiness assessment.
Determine the most appropriate Medi-Cal behavioral health pathway for Phoenix.
Develop a comprehensive certification/contracting and implementation roadmap.
Lead preparation and submission of required applications and supporting materials.
Interface with applicable county and state agencies.
Design the behavioral health division's organizational structure.
Develop the clinical and administrative staffing model.
Develop required policies, procedures, compliance systems, and operational protocols.
Assist with selection and implementation of an appropriate Electronic Health Record (EHR) and billing infrastructure.
Develop initial and long-term operating budgets and financial projections.
Evaluate reimbursement and financial sustainability.
Establish quality assurance and performance-measurement systems.
Assist with recruitment of key clinical and administrative leadership.
Guide Phoenix through certification/approval, implementation, and operational launch.

Ideal Background Strong candidates may have previous experience as a:
Behavioral Health Executive
County Behavioral Health Administrator
FQHC Executive
Chief Behavioral Health Officer
Healthcare COO/CEO
Director of Behavioral Health
Medi-Cal Behavioral Health Consultant
Healthcare Certification/Compliance Executive
Behavioral Health Program Development Consultant

Experience specifically involving California Specialty Mental Health Services, county Mental Health Plans, Medi-Cal behavioral health, CalAIM, DHCS requirements, and transition-age youth
is highly desirable.
Contract Structure This is a contractual, project-based engagement
, not a traditional full-time position.
Phoenix anticipates structuring the engagement around defined phases, deliverables, and milestones. The selected individual or firm may perform portions of the work remotely but must be available for in-person meetings, regulatory activities, implementation work, and leadership meetings as required.
Compensation will be negotiated based upon experience, proposed scope of work, project structure, and demonstrated ability to successfully complete the engagement.
What Success Looks Like Phoenix is not seeking a consultant who simply produces a feasibility report or policy manual.
We are seeking an experienced professional who can help us build the program.

The objective of this engagement is to take Phoenix from its current position through program design, regulatory approval/certification, implementation, and ultimately the successful launch of a sustainable behavioral health services operation.
Applying Applicants should submit a résumé/CV and a brief description of their relevant experience.
Applicants must also answer the following question:

Describe a California Medi-Cal mental health or behavioral health program that you personally helped develop from concept through application/certification or approval and operational launch. Identify your specific role in preparing the application, navigating the regulatory process, implementing the program, and managing or supporting operations after approval.

Please include the approximate year of the project, type of program/certification or approval obtained, regulatory or contracting agencies involved, and your specific responsibilities.
Phoenix Transitional Housing Plus is particularly interested in experienced professionals who are excited by the opportunity to help build an innovative behavioral health model specifically designed around the needs of transition-age youth and young adults.

jobs.description:
Title:
Program Director, CERC
Reports to:
Executive Director of National Service Programs
Salary Range:
$95,000-$103,000 annual salary, depending on qualifications & experience
Status:
Full-Time, Exempt
Location:
Hybrid - San Francisco Bay Area. Can work remotely, but spontaneous travel will be required throughout California and for occasional meetings in the BACR office in El Cerrito, CA.

Benefits:

Core benefits: Medical, wellness/mental health benefit, dental, vision, life insurance, FSA (medical, dependent, transit), hospital indemnity, retirement, WellHub, employee assistance program
Additional Perks: wellness fair, people-centered work culture, ability to make an impact in your community through mission-driven work.
Time off: Include vacation, sick, 15 holidays, parental and medical leave policy, and mental health days
Growth: Include conference opportunities, regular training opportunities, and professional development week

Roles and Responsibilities:

Strategic Planning

The Program Director is responsible for guiding CERC (California Emergency Response Corps) to fulfill its mission in the best way possible by working with the staff to form plans of approach for various challenges. Some of the areas where this planning is needed are:
Recruitment, Selection and Retention of ACMs
Recruitment and Selection of Staff
Expansion/Reduction of the program
Deployments
Training for Staff and ACM’s
CERC’s relationship with BACR and California Volunteers (CV)
Improvement of internal processes and procedures (e.g. Salesforce development)

Agency Partner and Other Relationships

The Program Director has a lead role in developing and maintaining relationships with CERC partners and other Community Based Organizations. These responsibilities include:
Recruiting new and potential Partner Agencies
Planning events with partner agencies (e.g. site supervisor orientation)
Quarterly site visits with Project Coordinators
When necessary, act as mediator when issues arise between agencies and ACMs or agencies and the program
Participating in BACR Leaders Group
Streamlining communication between BACR, CERC, and CV

Contracts/Development

The Program Director is responsible for all regular reports and all funding proposals to Government Agencies, BACR, and other organizations and foundations that provide funding to CERC.

Fiscal Management

The Program Director is also responsible for making sure the program as a whole does not exceed its budget. On a day-to-day basis this means the Program Director is responsible for:
Approving expenses/purchases
Approving staff time sheets
Salary review

Deployment Management and Supervision

The Program Director is responsible for responding to all deployment requests from California Volunteers. This includes budget management; program coordinator and ACM assignments; and managing relationships with requesting partners. The Program Director is responsible for deployment supervision, which will require spontaneous travel for on the ground supervision.

Management

The Program Director is the Supervisor for all CERC Staff and directly supervises the following positions:
Project Coordinators
AmeriCorps Members

Identify needs and responsibilities of Project Coordinators and provide necessary support, coaching and supervision. This includes, but is not limited to:
Regular Check-ins with all Project Coordinators
Observe and give feedback to Project Coordinators regarding Team days, Trainings, and other facets of their job and overall job performance
Conduct performance evaluations for Project Coordinators
Act as an Advocate/Problem Solver for Project Coordinators in issues involving ACM’s, CERC and BACR Leadership, and Agency Partners
Responsible for reviewing and auditing ACM files
Make sure that Project Coordinators fulfill their responsibilities, both those that are part of their job description and any other responsibilities they may have taken on
Help Project Coordinators to work effectively by working with them to establish clear and specific steps toward fulfilling their goals, and following up on those steps
Keep secure files with necessary paperwork for each Project Coordinator
When possible, provide training and professional development opportunities

CERC Organizational Requirements

All CERC staff have certain responsibilities which are necessary to be an effective part of the CERC team. The Program Director is responsible for:
Approving (signing) BACR paperwork for Staff (expense reports, check requests, staff time sheets, etc.)
Timely submission of paperwork as deemed necessary by BACR
Taking the lead in strategic planning and visioning for CERC as a whole
Attendance & participation in Staff and Corps Member Trainings and Events
Willingness to take on additional responsibilities when necessary and feasible

Preferred Qualifications:

Minimum of 5 years of broad experience in managing and developing programs
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to interact effectively with other community agencies
Ability to work independently while remaining engaged in a strong, mutually respectful team
Clear, friendly and professional public speaking manner
Excellent writing skills
Willingness to work weekends and/or evenings
Knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Access) and Salesforce
Ability to handle multiple projects and prioritize.
Must have their own vehicle and provide car insurance.

Personal Characteristics:

The Director should embody the following personal characteristics:
Have a passion for service
Good judgment and consensus-building skills
Self-confidence
Inspiring, creative, and compassionate
Diplomatic and tactful
High ethical standards
Values diversity
Sense of humor

Education:

Bachelor's or advanced degree in nonprofit management, business administration, or related field.

VMGROUPE is a full-service agency that operates as an extension of clients’ internal teams, focused on creating desire and driving transformative growth for leading and high-profile brands. The agency specializes in luxury sectors including beauty, fashion, jewelry, horology, fragrances, fine foods, wine & spirits, real estate, automotive, aviation, tourism, and hospitality. In a highly digital landscape, VMGROUPE delivers exceptional branding, memorable content, compelling storytelling, and high-conversion campaigns. Since 2006, the team has been elevating brands through strategic insight, creative excellence, and a deep understanding of premium and luxury markets.

Role Description

The Managing Director is the operating force behind VMGROUPE, turning vision into momentum, standards into systems, and ambition into sustainable growth. We are seeking an experienced agency leader to direct the day-to-day performance of the business and ensure every department, client relationship, and workstream operates with clarity, accountability, and excellence. Reporting to the Founder and Chief Creative Officer, you will lead the agency across account management, creative, strategy, production, social, communications, performance marketing, finance, people operations, and new business. You will translate the agency’s vision into operating priorities, ensuring teams understand what matters, who owns it, and how success will be measured. You will own the health of the agency across revenue, profitability, client satisfaction, team performance, resource planning, operational efficiency, and quality of delivery. You will create the structure that allows VMGROUPE to scale without losing its standards, culture, creative edge, or humanity. This role requires a decisive operator, trusted client partner, commercial thinker, and emotionally intelligent leader who can hold the full picture while remaining close to the work.

You will serve as the agency’s central point of alignment, balancing commercial performance, creative ambition, client trust, and team wellbeing. By strengthening leadership accountability, anticipating risks, and improving how decisions are made, you will create the conditions for VMGROUPE to grow with discipline, consistency, and confidence. This role requires a decisive operator, trusted client partner, commercial thinker, and emotionally intelligent leader who remains close to the work while maintaining command of the whole.

You are:

You are a seasoned agency leader who knows how to lead people, protect relationships, strengthen operations, and drive commercial performance.
You bring order to complexity without slowing momentum. You see risks early, address issues directly, and create clear paths forward. You understand when a team needs direction, when a leader needs support, and when a decision needs to be made.
You are commercially astute and creatively fluent. You understand the financial mechanics of an agency and the conditions required for exceptional work. You know how scopes, staffing, timelines, margins, client expectations, and team morale influence one another.
You lead with authority without creating fear. You set high standards, communicate with precision, and hold people accountable with fairness and consistency.
You are comfortable advising a founder, leading senior executives, presenting to clients, resolving conflict, reviewing financial performance, shaping a proposal, and stepping into a complex project when leadership is required.
You do not wait for problems to become visible. You build the systems that prevent them.

Qualifications

10+ years demonstrated leadership experience in agency, consultancy, or brand-side environments, with a focus on luxury, premium, or high-profile brands.
Proven track record in strategic planning, brand development, and integrated marketing across digital and traditional channels.
Strong client relationship management skills, including experience managing executive-level stakeholders and complex, multi-market accounts.
Operational management capabilities, including budgeting, resource planning, performance measurement, and process optimization.
Experience driving new business opportunities, pitching concepts, and closing strategic partnerships.
Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate complex ideas clearly and persuasively.
Collaborative leadership style, with a commitment to developing talent, promoting inclusion, and maintaining a positive team culture.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, or a related field; advanced degree or equivalent experience is beneficial.
Comfort working in a hybrid environment in New York, NY, with the ability to manage in-person and remote teams effectively.
Experience working with brands in sectors such as beauty, fashion, jewelry, fragrances, fine foods, wine & spirits, real estate, automotive, aviation, tourism, or hospitality is a strong plus.

jobs.description:
Description

African American Planning Commission, Inc.

Assistant Director- Renee Steedley Family Residence

The African American Planning Commission Inc. (AAPCI)
is a nonprofit organization founded in 1996, committed to reducing homelessness and addressing the related issues of domestic violence, HIV/AIDS, mental illness, substance abuse, shortage of affordable housing, and unemployment in the communities in which we live and serve.

AAPCI has grown exponentially — from a dedicated staff of one, with nothing but a vision and a zero operating budget, working out of borrowed office space in 1996, to 35 full and part-time employees in 2014. Services include the provision of three hot meals and snacks each day, 24-hour shelter, social supportive services, employment preparation services, and housing placement assistance as well as crisis case management services.

We’re completely committed to building and maintaining a great organizational culture that involves active employees – people looking to give back to the community, wanting to inspire creativity in others and motivate and empower one another.

Reporting Relationships:
Assistant Directors report to the Program Director

Position Summary:
This position is responsible for managing the administrative functions of the residence to ensure compliance with government regulations, effective administrative support to programs and efficient interaction with other facility departments.

Nature and Scope:
The incumbent serves as a part of the senior administrative team at this facility, with significant input into policy decisions affecting the facility as a whole. The incumbent is also an important resource to co-workers in administrative areas, including information management, personnel practices and systems design. The incumbent facilitates problem-solving between units of the facility, other departments of serenity House and government agencies.

Principal Duties And Responsibilities

Under the general supervision of the Program Director, Assistant Directors are expected to perform the following principal duties and responsibilities;

Supervise administrative support to program staff, ensuring efficient program operation and achievement of program goals.
Oversee vacancy control, including coordination with the facility’s maintenance and operations units and city agencies, to ensure maximal revenue consistent with program goals and eligibility criteria.
Administer on-site fiscal functions, including invoicing of receivables, control of petty cash and review of financial reports to ensure fiscal accountability, timely receipt of revenue, accuracy of financial records, compliance with funding source guidelines and adherence to Serenity House policies and procedures.
Administer attendance, payroll and other onsite human resources’ functions to ensure that personnel receive appropriate compensation and benefits and that recruitment, hiring and termination of personnel is processed in a prompt and effective manner.
Act as chief facility liaison to government funding agencies, Homeless services liaison, to Serenity House support departments and the Assistant Administrator of Administration and Finance, Homeless Services, facilitating effective communication, compliance with reporting requirements, accurate record keeping and the timely and efficient processing of program needs.
Initiate, plan, implement, assist with and follow-up on special projects to meet ad-hoc demands upon the facility and its Director.
Ensure maximum productivity and development of staff by managing human resources’ functions for the administrative unit.
Plan, develop and implement administrative support policies and procedures, ensuring uniformity of service within the Division, compliance with Tier II Regulatory Agencies and synchronization with other facility service units.
Oversee the timely collection, preparation and analysis of administrative, client and program information to generate reports and memos, evaluate program performance and determine unmet needs.
As a member of the interdisciplinary administrative team, participate in the development of facility policies, procedures and programming and function as an administrative team member to enhance overall service provisions and inter-unit staff collaboration.

Qualifications

Minimal Qualifications

Degree Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in an appropriate social service field or administration.
At least five (5) years administrative office management experience
At least two (2) years of supervisory experience and office management systems.
Knowledge of data base management systems, word processing, local area networks, bookkeeping, public relations and grant procurement is necessary.

Other Qualifications

Strong verbal and interpersonal communication skills with focus on providing excellent client services.

Strong written communication skills and ability to complete reports, as assigned

Demonstrate ability to interact effectively and collaboratively with a diverse community of residents, program staff and external vendors.

Ability to exercise good judgment and apply problem solving skills.

Experience working collaboratively in a team oriented and outcomes focused environment.

Physical Requirements

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer

Must be able to lift to 5 pounds at times

Must be able to access and navigate each department at the organization’s facilities

About The Role

We provide our clients with a comprehensive suite of strategic communications services that leverage our integrated offering, including financial communications, corporate reputation, transaction communications and public affairs in all the major markets around the world.

Our Retail and Consumer Products sector team is growing quickly and we are looking for a Managing Director to be a key leader in establishing our Public Affairs offering, driving that growth by leveraging their own network and contributing to sector development initiatives. The ideal candidate has strong capabilities in developing business, which is underpinned by a public affairs background. This person will both leverage their own book of business to help lead business development efforts while also handling day-to-day management of client accounts and firm initiatives.

A successful Managing Director will be responsible for bringing in business, leading and growing business with current clients, managing teams, and take a key role in pursuits. This individual will interact with and provide communications counsel to C-suite, corporate affairs and communications executives; develop and execute integrated communications strategies to deliver results and meet client expectations; review and draft a variety of materials for client use; and actively participate in firm development and new business pursuits to help grow the sector. Coaching and mentoring early and mid-career colleagues is an important part of the Managing Director role to ensure all team members have the skills and tools to perform well at their level.
